absent: Vendor specific load and put behavior beyond the delegation point.
Performance counter cleanup and event servicing after the request is raised.
Clock, timer migration, and steal update handling after requests are raised.
Emulation context layout and register cache writeback mechanics.
Raw register accessor implementation and instruction pointer and flags handling.
Userspace register structure layout and error code ABI beyond invalid argument on protected state.
Nested address translation and guest page read failure modes.
Shadow root lifetime and MMU reload sequencing after page pointer changes.
Steal time control bit definitions and guest structure layout beyond the preempted byte.
Xen long mode detection and runstate cache activation and teardown lifecycle.
Branch barrier, protection key, and time stamp counter hardware semantics.
Rate limiting policy governing global versus local clock updates.

findings.text: Userspace request to fetch general registers first refuses protected guests with an invalid argument failure, otherwise it pins the virtual CPU, gathers register state through an internal helper, releases the pin, and reports success.

Userspace request to install general registers first refuses protected guests, otherwise it pins the virtual CPU, applies register state through an internal helper, releases the pin, and reports success.

Fetching synchronizes from emulation only when a pending to vcpu flag is set, clearing it after writeback to support mid emulation reads, while installing always marks need from vcpu and clears need to vcpu to force later resynchronization.

Both directions cover the classic general set plus instruction pointer and flags, with extra extended registers on sixty four bit builds; installing forces a fixed flags bit, clears pending exception state in two trackers, and requests event processing.
Stack pointer access in both directions goes through a raw register channel selected by a stack pointer selector, matching the treatment of other general registers.

Loading records the calling physical CPU, publishes the virtual CPU as running on this CPU, subscribes its preemption notifier, invokes architecture specific loading, then unpins the CPU; putting disables preemption, invokes architecture specific putting, unsubscribes the notifier, clears the running marker, then reenables preemption.

Architecture loading requests a speculative buffer flush, handles performance counter cleanup when rescheduled with counts, handles writeback cache emulation, delegates to vendor loading, manages branch predictor isolation and host protection key saving, reconciles time stamp counter state and timers, and always requests steal time refresh.

Whether writeback emulation is needed depends solely on a nonzero noncoherent DMA counter for the virtual machine; when needed the path either records dirtiness for the current CPU if exits are available or flushes the previous CPU when the virtual CPU moved.

Suspend induced offset corrections are scaled and applied once then cleared with a clock update request; on CPU change or unstable clock the code measures host counter delta, flags backwards motion, rebuilds guest offset from last guest value and enables catchup unless protected, restarts hypervisor timers, chooses global or local clock refresh with rate limiting, requests timer migration, and remembers the new CPU.
Host offset adjustment is scaled by the level one ratio before being applied to the guest, with a warning if a negative correction arrives while a nondefault ratio is active.

When the virtual CPU differs from the last one on that physical CPU a branch prediction barrier is issued subject to a static key and the last marker is updated; host protection key state is saved on every load and a steal update is always requested.

Architecture putting, only when the virtual CPU was preempted, derives an in kernel flag from protected state or privilege level, holds a sleepable read lock while updating either Xen runstate or steal time, then delegates to vendor putting and records the current host counter.

Marking preempted requires an instruction boundary and several guards including enabled control, not already marked, matching process address space, and fresh valid address cache; on success a single byte is written to guest memory without fault, a cached flag is set, and the backing slot page is dirtied.
One build enables Xen controls only when both a global feature key and a per VM model flag are true, while an alternate build always reports disabled, giving a configuration dependent predicate.
Xen preempted handling asserts the preempted marker and then moves the runstate accounting to runnable through the shared updater.

Runstate starts from offline on first use, ignores negative clock deltas except for baseline refresh, attributes scheduler delay to runnable when previously running with capping, accumulates remaining time to the prior state, refreshes entry time, and mirrors to guest when a cache is active.

Guest mirroring selects native or compat sizing from build width and guest long mode, derives total length and time origin, uses one page mapping normally and two when crossing a page boundary, and revalidates mappings before writing.

Both runstate variants place a same sized state word at the start, followed by a sixty four bit entry time and then four sixty four bit counters matching internal storage; compat totals forty four bytes while native adds four bytes of shift after the first word.

Top bit of the entry time signals an update in progress and lives in the final byte of that word on little endian; the high byte equals 128 and the protocol sets it before the body and clears it after with ordering barriers.

Guest cache updates hold a read lock with interrupts saved, retrying with refresh when invalid; atomic callers use try acquisition and give up without sleeping, while split mappings nest second inside first with a distinct subclass and restart validation from the beginning after any drop.

Preempted bookkeeping holds a sleepable read lock across generation checks, loading pins the CPU across publishing and architecture work, and putting holds preemption disabled across architecture work and notifier removal.

Page directory pointer loading translates the address for nested guests, reads four entries at a thirty two byte aligned offset, rejects present entries with reserved bits, rebuilds shadow roots when changed without direct paging, stores the copy, marks the register dirty, requests MMU reload, clears a userspace origin flag, and signals success with one versus zero on failure.
Reserved checks combine per VM reserved address bits with bit ranges five to eight and one to two.

Guests may place the runstate area unaligned and crossing pages with unaligned sixty four bit fields in compat mode, requiring stack bounce and dual copy; native padding must be cleared to avoid exposing kernel bytes.

Register access fails for protected guests, steal marking is skipped on address space mismatch or stale cache, backwards host counters mark time unstable, and scaled negative adjustments trigger a warning.

Several helpers serve as cross file interfaces for register ioctls, virtual CPU pinning, architecture load and put, DMA coherence query, Xen runstate refresh, page pointer loading, and guest cache dirty marking.
Dirty marking asserts its cache lock is held and does nothing without a memory slot, otherwise dirties the slot page for the cached guest address.

Compat runstate totals forty four bytes and native totals forty eight bytes, state starts at offset zero, entry time immediately precedes the time array by eight bytes, and the time array matches four eight byte counters.
